newsitem.title: USA: Frontier Airlines sees Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Frontier Airlines sees Q2 loss.

text.p: Frontier Airlines Inc said on Wednesday that it expected to show a loss for its second fiscal quarter due to sluggish traffic, higher fuel costs and the reinstatement of a 10 percent federal ticket tax.

Frontier president and chief executive officer Sam Addoms said that despite the company's positive performance in July and August, slow traffic during September "wiped out our gains for the prior months and produced a revenue shortfall for the full quarter."
The high cost of "wet leasing" an aircraft to replace one in a regularly scheduled maintenance cycle was also expected to hurt the quarter, the company said.
Addoms said it was too early to determine the extent of the second quarter loss, but said the company had record net profits totalling $2.2 million in the prior two quarters.
He said the company was working on a number of programs to improve its future performance, including a corporate travel program to increase Frontier's share of the business market.

The company's planned fleet additions would also produce some sizeable economies of scale, Addoms said. Frontier was also studying ways to reduce its distribution costs through a less expensive computer reservation system, he said.
The company had cash on the balance sheet of $19 million, which included funds for additional jet leases, he said.
